newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Friday were seen steady-$1.00 per cwt higher, lifted by keen competition for tight supplies, livestock dealers said.

The thin supply of hogs was linked to seasonal declines in market hog numbers exacerbated by increased fieldwork in Illinois, Indiana and Ohio which leaves farmers little time to sell hogs, sources said.
But hogs being held back by plantings were not said to be in large numbers judging from weights in the eastern Corn Belt that indicate farmers have stayed current, they said.
One major hog dealer in the eastern Belt said weights were running normal at 240 to 250 lbs this week.

Weights in the western Belt, however, suggested hogs there were held back by producers, market sources said. Iowa/ southern Minnesota barrow and gilt hog weights last week averaged 253.4 lbs, up from 252.7 lbs the previous week and above 248.7 a year ago, USDA statistics showed.
USDA estimated the average slaughter hog weight last week at 256 lbs, the same as a week earlier and up one lb from a year earlier.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices at the plant were seen ranging from $57.50 to $58.00 and Illinois top prices could range $58.00 to $58.50 at the plant, sources in those areas said. Indiana and Ohio top hog prices could range $56.00-$58.00, dealers and packer buyers there said.
